title: Sizzling! UK Hits 30.5°C and It's Only Going to Get Hotter!
summary: Wow, it's a scorcher! On Saturday, the UK baked under the hottest day of the year so far. The temperature hit 30.5°C (that's about 87°F) in Frittenden, Kent. That's hotter than the day before, which was already a toasty 28.4°C in London. And guess what? It's going to get even hotter over the long weekend! Weather experts say Monday could be the hottest May day ever recorded in the UK, with temperatures possibly reaching 33°C or even 34°C. That would smash the old record of 32.8°C set way back in 1944. Because of the heat, amber alerts are in place for parts of England. That means the heat could be dangerous, especially for kids and people over 65. The rest of England has yellow alerts, so everyone should be careful. The good news? After some cloudy days, Scotland and Northern Ireland will get sunny and warm too, with Glasgow maybe hitting the mid-20s. But if you're heading to the east coast of England, watch out for mist! This early heatwave is a sign of our changing climate. So, whether you're at a medieval jousting show or just chilling in a park, stay cool, drink lots of water, and slap on that sunscreen!
why_it_matters: When the weather gets extremely hot, it can be dangerous for kids playing outside and for older relatives, so knowing how to stay safe—like drinking water and using sunscreen—helps us all enjoy summer without getting sick.

background_read: The UK usually has mild summers, so a temperature of 30°C is rare and can strain hospitals and power supplies. In 1944, during World War II, the previous May record of 32.8°C was set.
Today, scientists say climate change is making extreme heat events like this more likely. The Met Office, the UK’s national weather service, issues amber and yellow alerts to warn people of danger.
Frittenden is a small village in Kent, in southeastern England, where the first day’s high temperature was recorded.
